questions.question: It is July in BC. Which is more likely: rain or snow?
questions.explain: In July it is too warm for snow, so rain is more likely. Snow comes in winter, not summer.

questions.question: You walk to school in the morning. Which is less likely: a dog or a bear?
questions.explain: Bears are very rare on a walk to school, so a bear is less likely. Dogs are common near homes and parks.

questions.question: You open your lunchbox at school. Which is more likely: a sandwich or a cake?
questions.explain: Most days you pack a sandwich, so it is more likely. You only get cake on a special day like a birthday.

questions.question: You look out the window on a rainy day. Which is less likely: a puddle or a rainbow?
questions.explain: Puddles happen every rainy day, but rainbows only come out sometimes. A rainbow is less likely than a puddle.

questions.question: Mia has 3 red marbles and 1 blue marble in her jar. She picks one at random. Which is more likely: red or blue?
questions.explain: There are 3 red marbles but only 1 blue one, so red is more likely. More marbles of a colour makes it more likely to be picked.

questions.question: You have a bag with 4 socks and 1 hat. You close your eyes and pick one. Which is more likely: a sock or a hat?
questions.explain: There are 4 socks but only 1 hat, so a sock is more likely. More of one thing in the bag makes it more likely to come out.

questions.question: Your friend has 2 chocolate bars and 5 candy bars in his lunch. He picks one to share. Which is less likely: chocolate or candy?
questions.explain: There are only 2 chocolate bars but 5 candy bars, so chocolate is less likely. Fewer of one thing makes it less likely to be picked.

questions.question: In the park you see 8 red flowers and 2 white flowers. You pick one at random. Which is more likely: white or red?
questions.explain: There are 8 red flowers but only 2 white ones, so red is more likely. White is the one you might wish for, but red is more common.

questions.question: Tom has 5 green blocks and 2 red blocks. He takes out 1 green block. Now he picks one at random. Which colour is more likely: green or red?
questions.explain: After taking 1 green, Tom has 4 green and 2 red. Green is still more likely because there are still more green blocks left.

questions.question: Sara puts 4 stars and 2 moons on her wall. Her sister adds 1 more moon. Now Sara picks one shape at random. Which is less likely: a star or a moon?
questions.explain: After adding 1 moon there are 4 stars and 3 moons. Stars are still more common, so a moon is less likely to be picked.

questions.question: Lily says: I have 2 red balls and 5 blue balls. I pick one. Red is more likely because I like red best. What went wrong?
options: She swapped more and less around
Blue is always more likely here
She went by liking, not counting
She should pick two to be sure
questions.explain: Lily chose red because she likes it, but 5 blue means blue is actually more likely. You count the balls, not your wishes.

questions.question: A tin has 6 stickers and 2 erasers. Ben takes 2 stickers out. Now he picks one item at random. Which is more likely: a sticker or an eraser?
questions.explain: After taking 2 stickers, Ben has 4 stickers and 2 erasers. Stickers are still more likely because there are more of them left in the tin.
